items.subject: System Design
items.body: Question 1 of 5: Explain the difference between Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading) and Write-Through caching strategies. When would you choose one over the other in a high-throughput SDE architecture?

metadata.modelAnswer: In Cache-Aside, the app first checks the cache. On a miss, it fetches from DB, writes to cache, and returns. In Write-Through, writes update the cache and DB simultaneously, guaranteeing consistency.

rubric.structure: Clear definition of Cache-Aside followed by Write-Through and a comparison trade-off.
rubric.specificity: Mentions cache miss flow, database latency, write performance, and consistency guarantees.

items.subject: Computer Science
items.body: Question 2 of 5: How do you find two numbers in a sorted array that add up to a target sum in O(N) time and O(1) extra space? Explain your approach and edge cases.

metadata.modelAnswer: Initialize left pointer at index 0 and right pointer at length - 1. Calculate sum. If sum < target, left++. If sum > target, right--. If sum == target, return pointers.

rubric.structure: Pointers initialization -> While loop condition -> Target comparison -> Complexity bound.
rubric.specificity: States O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space clearly.

items.subject: Behavioral Competency
items.body: Question 3 of 5: Behavioral: Describe a situation where you had a technical disagreement with a team member on a project architecture. Frame your response using the STAR method.

metadata.modelAnswer: STAR: Situation (teammate wanted NoSQL while I preferred Postgres), Task (needed alignment), Action (ran benchmark load test), Result (Postgres proved 40% faster for transactions).

rubric.structure: Follows explicit Situation -> Task -> Action -> Result narrative sequence.
rubric.specificity: Uses empirical benchmarking data rather than subjective opinion to resolve conflict.

items.subject: Business Analytics
items.body: Question 4 of 5: How would you calculate Month-1 User Retention Rate in SQL for an e-commerce platform? Describe the required joins and aggregation logic.

metadata.modelAnswer: Join user signup cohort table with active monthly orders table. Filter for active order month = signup month + 1. Calculate Retention % = (M1 Users / Total Cohort) * 100.

rubric.structure: Identifies signup cohort -> Specifies join on user_id -> Filters M1 date -> Formulates percentage ratio.
rubric.specificity: Mentions exact SQL date functions or month differences.

items.subject: Software Engineering
items.body: Question 5 of 5: What is Idempotency in HTTP REST APIs, and how do you ensure an API endpoint (like payment processing) is safe against duplicate requests?

metadata.modelAnswer: An idempotent request produces the same result no matter how many times it is executed. For payments, pass a unique Idempotency-Key header stored in Redis to block duplicate charges.

rubric.structure: Defines Idempotency -> Explains duplicate risk in retries -> Proposes Idempotency-Key header solution.
rubric.specificity: Mentions unique transaction UUIDs, atomic locking, and HTTP 200 vs 409 status codes.
